content:
According to 9to5Mac's web traffic analysis, Apple is testing iOS 27.0.1 for iPhone. The update is expected to focus on bug fixes and performance improvements.

iOS 27.0.1 is coming soon

9to5Mac's analytics data began showing traces of iOS 27.0.1 a few days ago, and MacRumors has also reported on it.

Citing Apple this morning, 9to5Mac reported that a software update will be released early next week to address an issue causing some iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max devices to automatically reboot after a failed Face ID authentication.

We reported on this issue a few days ago, explaining that it occurs when you use Face ID to unlock apps like Passwords. If Face ID fails, your iPhone may unexpectedly restart.

I've been unable to reproduce this issue on my own iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, but clearly a significant number of users are affected. The good news is that this is a bug that can be fixed via software, not a hardware fault.

While nothing is confirmed, iOS 27.0.1 will very likely address the issue mentioned above. It may also include other bug fixes affecting iOS 27 and the new iPhone 18 Pro hardware.

Have you encountered any issues since upgrading to iOS 27? Any iPhone 18 Pro-specific problems? Let us know in the comments.
